Subject: Mutual action & eval plan: deployment mode + region decision for BrightLane

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the call earlier — it was helpful to map BrightLane's constraints (PHI residency in EU, low-latency inference on triage flows, and procurement window in July). I promised to send an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a short evaluation plan to help you compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments across the EU/US tradeoffs.

Attached: BrightLane_MAP_v1.pdf (outline MAP + timelines).

High-level proposal: 
- Evaluation scope: 2-week technical POC comparing Hosted (eu-west region) vs Dedicated reserved capacity (eu-west) vs a checklist for Private (on-prem/VPC) feasibility.
- Success criteria: 99th percentile inference latency < 250ms for triage model under 50 RPS, token cost delta < 2x, and documented security posture for PHI.
- Timeline target: complete evaluation & choose deployment mode by 2026-07-15 to align with procurement.

Next steps for this week:
1) BrightLane to confirm preferred EU regions and up to 3 sample endpoints (we can run synthetic and replay).
2) Redwood to stand up a hosted trial in eu-west and provide quick dedicated-estimate sizing + cost.
3) Legal/procurement to share contract milestones — Rafael/Laura will coordinate with your procurement lead.

I CC'd Laura (enterprise contracts) and Priyom (solutions) to help with the SLA/pricing draft and the technical runbook. Can we lock a 30-min checkpoint on Thursday?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rafael — thanks for the summary and the MAP. Quick notes from our side: 
- We must keep PHI within EU by default; however, we can consider US region only for non-PHI logs and telemetry.
- Performance: our triage path needs < 250ms p99 for 10-50 RPS; peak could spike to 80 RPS during mornings.
- Procurement: target contract sign by 7/20; we can accelerate but need pricing and an initial SOW by 7/8.

Attaching our procurement timeline and a short list of technical contacts.

Can Redwood provide: 
1) a short performance baseline for hosted eu-west (p50/p95/p99) on the suggested model family;
2) clear differences in support and uptime SLAs between Hosted and Dedicated;
3) a checklist for Private deployment (networking/KMS/audit logs) and rough delivery lead time.

We'll confirm the three sample endpoints by Tuesday.

Thanks,
Marta Sokol
VP Product, BrightLane Health

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-06-16T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Mutual action & eval plan: deployment mode + region decision for BrightLane

Rafael / team — quick internal notes to prepare the POC and the decision matrix: 
- Hosted (eu-west): fastest to run; we can spin a test endpoint within 48 hours. Expect p99 around 180-240ms for the medium-sized LLM (light quantization) at 50 RPS with continuous batching. Need to validate with BrightLane sample payloads (prefix lengths).
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and isolated capacity; reserve 4 GPU cards (8k context) for triage flows to hold p99 < 200ms at 50-80 RPS. We should provide a cost delta estimate: roughly 1.6–2.1x hosted unit cost (depending on commit/term).
- Private: significant onboarding (network peering, KMS, audit log transfer); delivery lead ~6-8 weeks, higher fixed engineering effort. Good for strict data control but higher TCO.

Action items for the MAP: technical acceptance criteria (latency/cost/security), who signs-off on each gate, and the sample replay payloads. I will prepare a short latency-cost CSV and a checklist for Private readiness.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Decision gate: choose deployment mode by 2026-07-15; procurement to have pricing/SOW by 2026-07-08.
